Gibraltar: Companies Act 2014 (as amended), including foreign-company provisions; Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; Sanctions Act 2019; Financial Services Commission AML/CFT Guidance Notes (current edition); Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2019.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, shareholders and authorized signatories must be screened before incorporation and on an ongoing quarterly basis against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, HM Treasury consolidated list, OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated financial sanctions, Gibraltar domestic sanctions list, Bermuda domestic sanctions list, and the FATF list of high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions. Politically Exposed Persons, including family members and close associates, must be classified according to a mandatory risk-based PEP assessment; any PEP match requires senior management approval, enhanced source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Because the commercial model monetizes through Apple App Store and Google Play payouts, the compliance protocol must also apply multi-jurisdiction payment-beneficiary watchlist filtering, including CJK transliteration and alias screening, to prevent sanctioned App Store seller identity and prohibited country access.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (Companies and Professional Entities Registry) via approved Bermuda Corporate Service Providers; secondary coordination for any Gibraltar branch establishment must be made through Gibraltar Companies House online name reservation at www.companieshouse.gi
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory company names must be expressed in Latin/Roman alphabetic script and may use English or a Romanized transliteration of a foreign name. Punctuation is limited to the full stop, comma, hyphen, plus sign, ampersand and apostrophe. The name must end with a permissible corporate identifier such as 'Limited' or the approved abbreviation 'Ltd.' in the case of the Bermuda Exempted Company. Any name containing Chinese, Japanese, Korean or other non-Latin script must be submitted with a certified English/Roman-script transliteration, and the registered legal name will be that transliteration only.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In Bermuda, if the Registrar of Companies rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration within 14 days under section 13(3) of the Companies Act 1981. A further refusal may be challenged by judicial review proceedings before the Supreme Court of Bermuda. In Gibraltar, a name rejection by Companies House Gibraltar may be contested by filing a formal written objection with the Registrar within 21 days, followed by judicial review before the Supreme Court of Gibraltar if the registry maintains the rejection. The appeal must restate the proposed name, identify the statutory basis, explain why the name is not misleading prohibited or confusing, and provide an alternative Romanized transliteration if relevant. A name reservation may not be extended beyond the 30-day validity window, but a new reservation application may be filed before expiration of the existing one.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Bermuda Exempted Company is statutorily required to maintain a physical registered office in Bermuda; a virtual mailbox alone cannot satisfy that obligation. The physical office may be the premises of the licensed corporate service provider, which is an accepted and common practice for Low-Risk standard software publishing. For any Gibraltar foreign-company branch or permanent establishment, a registered office or service address within Gibraltar is required; a pure virtual office is generally disfavored for AML record-keeping and may be rejected by the Gibraltar Companies House or financial institutions involved in Apple/Google payout collection unless supported by a physical compliance address and substantive record-keeping arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 3-5% annual risk of unannounced physical inspection for an unlicensed Bermuda Exempted Company operating solely as an MMORPG publisher; this rises to approximately 5-10% if a Gibraltar branch is registered; and to 15-25% if the same vehicle obtains a Gibraltar EMI relationship, holds customer funds, or adds regulated financial activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), sections 12-21 (incorporation and constitution), 58-91 (share capital), 165-190 (directors and company secretary), and 234-240 (registered office); supplemented by the Companies (Forms) Regulations 2014. The entity is constituted on the exempted-company model (Bermuda Exempted Company classification) with limited liability, no statutory minimum capital, and permitted non-resident ownership.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form F-01) followed by Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or capital deposit requirement; subscriber shares may be issued fully paid in the currency of denomination selected in the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation application is approved and that the initial share allotment, fully paid, be ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office be fixed at the Gibraltar registered agent's address, and that agent be appointed registered representative. RESOLVED FURTHER that [A] and [B] be appointed first directors, and [C] company secretary and money laundering reporting officer, each to hold office until replaced by ordinary resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors be authorized to execute any statutory filings, bank account forms, licence applications, and agreements to implement the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and constitutional structure pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Companies Registry online system to confirm the proposed company name is available and not deceptive. Submit a name reservation request, and pre-review the corporate structure, class of shares, director and shareholder profile.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or misleading, file a fresh reservation using an alternative name or appeal the decision by written representation to the Registrar under Companies Act 2014.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar registered agent and notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the Companies Act 2014; have all subscriber shareholders execute the documents; notarize the signatures and certify director consents and identity documents; deliver the execution pack to the Gibraltar registered agent for statutory vetting.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act as first directors
Identity, address and source-of-funds documents for beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or agent identifies a defect, cure by re-execution and re-notarization of the affected signature pages before submission to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the prescribed Form F-01 together with the executed constitutional documents, declarations of compliance, registered agent consent and payment of the statutory fee. Submit beneficial ownership and initial officer information as required by the Registry.
required_dossiers: Signed Form F-01 Application for Incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Declaration of compliance by subscriber or agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Registry clarification or technical query within 14 days; if the application is rejected, correct the flagged fields and resubmit within the same SLA cycle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory verification of the application, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and allocates the company registration number. Confirm the certificate details and request certified copies for bank and commercial counterparties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed, contact the Registry with the application reference; supply any additional evidence of authorized signatory to enable release of the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered office, statutory registers and beneficial ownership filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Gibraltar and Gibraltar registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Fix the registered office in Gibraltar at the approved agent address; maintain the statutory registers of members, directors, secretary and charges; file the initial beneficial ownership return under the Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2017; retain the registered agent as the point of official communications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rejected beneficial ownership filings must be corrected and refiled immediately to avoid default penalty; registrable errors in names, DOB or address are administrative corrections requiring no court application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolution and officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass the written first board resolution; approve the share allotment and registered office, appoint the first directors, company secretary and money laundering reporting officer, and authorize execution of operating and bank documents. Record the minutes and update the statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Signed pro forma first board resolution
Directors' and secretary's consents to act
Updated register of directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer appointment is challenged or disqualified, convene an alternate board/ordinary resolution and file the replacement appointment without delay.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to pure digital game publishing; residual contact point: Business Licensing Office, HM Government of Gibraltar
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial or trade licence is required for MMORPG publishing; no gambling licence is required where the game offers no real-money gaming or payout mechanics and monetization is limited to Apple and Google platform In-App Purchase.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 4: no EIA or environmental screening required for a non-physical software publishing operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core activity; the company must confirm that no wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste or manufacturing emissions are generated at its registered office. Any future physical site or outsourced data-centre operations must comply with Gibraltar's waste handling, disposal and environmental permitting thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial civil-defence or structural load clearance is required for a digital publisher with no plant or machinery. If a physical office is opened, fire safety certification under the Fire Safety Act 2003 (Gibraltar), a basic electrical installation inspection, and workplace health, safety and welfare clearance must be obtained before staff are deployed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (HM Government of Gibraltar; tax.gov.gi) is the competent authority for the Gibraltar jurisdiction. HMRC (gov.uk/hmrc) is the UK authority for any UK VAT or corporation tax nexus. The Bermuda Registrar of Companies (under the Bermuda Ministry of Finance) issues the Bermuda company registration number used as the entity TIN for CRS/FATCA and app-store tax forms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Bermuda Exempted Company with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies and obtain the Bermuda registration number (TIN) together with the Tax Assurance Certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, securing exemption from Bermuda taxes until 31 December 2035. Step 2: For Gibraltar, register the Bermuda company as an external company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Companies Act 2014) if a place of business or substance is established; file the corporate taxpayer application with the Income Tax Office to obtain the Gibraltar Tax Reference Number; a board resolution confirming that central management and control remains in Bermuda is required to support non-resident classification. Step 3: No Gibraltar VAT ID exists because Gibraltar has no VAT. Step 4: For the UK, no UK VAT registration is required while all UK consumer sales flow through Apple App Store and Google Play, as these platforms act as deemed suppliers; if the company were to make direct B2C digital supplies to UK consumers, it must register as a non-established taxable person with HMRC without any threshold. Step 5: Submit W-8BEN-E tax forms through App Store Connect and Google Play Console, quoting the Bermuda registration number and the Gibraltar Tax Reference Number for payout and withholding reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone. The Bermuda Exempted Company is exempt from Bermuda income, profits, dividends, and capital gains taxation until 2035. In Gibraltar, it is classified as a non-resident external company taxed on a territorial basis, so offshore MMORPG app-store revenue is outside Gibraltar source and therefore not assessable. UK corporate tax residence is avoided by ensuring central management and control remains in Bermuda and by having no UK permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Bermuda: election to apply for a Tax Assurance Certificate guaranteeing exemption from future Bermuda taxes until 31 December 2035. Gibraltar: no check-the-box election exists; tax residence follows central management and control under the Income Tax Act 2010, and the entity may secure non-resident status through factual substance in Bermuda. UK: the Hybrid and Other Mismatch Rules (TIOPA 2010 Part 6A) operate without elective filing for an opaque Bermuda body corporate; the entity is treated as opaque for both UK and Gibraltar purposes, and no hybrid mismatch election is available or required for app-store revenue flows.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No dedicated Gibraltar central bank exists. The United Kingdom's Bank of England anchors monetary policy and serves as the ultimate sterling liquidity backstop; HM Treasury (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation) retains UK-wide sanctions and exchange-control authority; the Government of Gibraltar issues Gibraltar Pound (GIP) notes under the Currency Notes Act; and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the prudential and licensing authority for all Gibraltar-licensed credit and payment institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Gibraltar/UK exchange-control framework imposes no general current-account or capital-account restrictions for corporate accounts, subject only to financial sanctions, AML/CFT verification, and reporting standards. The Gibraltar Pound is pegged to Pound Sterling at par and is freely issuable, but GIP is not a SWIFT-cleared international currency; the global treasury should execute settlement in GBP, EUR, USD and maintain only a working float in GIP. As a British Overseas Territory, Gibraltar does not hold separate IMF membership, but the United Kingdom's Article VIII obligations support full current-account convertibility for payments and transfers. Current-account flows, including Apple/Google in-app purchase proceeds, platform commissions, licensing fees, developer royalties, and profit remittances, are freely convertible and may be remitted without prior foreign-exchange approval, provided the underlying transaction is supported by a compliant evidentiary file. The capital account is also open: equity injections, shareholder loans, intercompany financing, dividends, and liquidation surplus movements may be freely credited to or debited from a Gibraltar account. For a Bermuda Exempted Company, there are no Gibraltar withholding-tax or exchange-control impediments to upstreaming profits because the entity is not Gibraltar-tax-resident if managed and controlled outside Gibraltar; however, a commercial bank may impose enhanced due diligence on distributions to establish ultimate beneficial ownership and to confirm that no UK/Gibraltar resident individual is using the offshore structure to evade tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender or conversion rules in Gibraltar or the United Kingdom. Export revenue, including digital in-app proceeds received from Apple App Store and Google Play payouts, may be retained in the original currency, converted wholly or partially to GBP/EUR/USD, or swept to a concentration account at treasury discretion. No minimum conversion ratio is mandated and no deadline exists for repatriation of foreign currency receipts into Gibraltar. The only mandatory operational controls are that proceeds clear through a licensed financial institution, the underlying sale/payout is accurately recorded in the accounting and transfer-pricing files, and the receiving bank is provided with an invoice or settlement report when the transaction is treated as an intercompany or treasury clearing flow.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account - segregated single-purpose account for inbound shareholder loan or equity injection
Operational Multi-Currency Account (GBP/EUR/USD) for MMORPG treasury and Apple/Google settlement
Operational Account / Treasury Concentration Account with same-day GBP and EUR clearing access via UK and EU correspondents
Corporate Clearing Account and standby LC facility for high-value operating or trade settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High for FCA-licensed UK and GFSC-licensed Gibraltar digital e-money institutions; Low for non-EEA, offshore-only EMIs that do not hold a post-Brexit European passport. A UK-authorised e-money institution may onboard the Bermuda Exempted Company with remote/virtual KYC, provide local-currency collection IBANs, and execute FX conversion; however, an EMI is not a bank and cannot provide a formally isolated capital escrow account, documentary credits, or bilateral treasury hedging. An offshore EMI without FCA or GFSC authorisation is legally barred from holding client money in Gibraltar or executing regulated payment services; such a service may be used only as a secondary collection utility with all funds ultimately settled through a licensed credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar tier-1 banks generally require at least one director or individually identifiable beneficial owner holding more than 25% of the entity to complete an in-person KYC interview at the Gibraltar branch or before a notary public in an apostille-recognised jurisdiction before the account is boarded. Remote opening is allowed only where the bank operates an approved video-verified account-opening framework, the company holds a substantial group relationship with that bank, or the KYC file is introduced by a global banking group under a delegated relationship manager. A Bermuda Exempted Company with non-resident beneficial owners and a nominee corporate director will be subject to a conclusive personal interview and a supplementary verification call with the economic owner; no tier-1 account should be structured on the basis of submission-only AML documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company presented as a nominee-veiled offshore company with a non-transparent beneficial ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the company's statutory registry bundle: Bermuda certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, register of members, register of directors, register of beneficial ownership, and annual return; current certificate of good standing from the Bermuda Registrar; apostilled copies of constitutional documents; notarised identification and address proof for every natural person with 10% or more beneficial interest; and a Bermuda-law legal opinion that identifies each beneficial owner and explains the legality of nominee arrangements, including any bearer-share prohibition and economic-substance compliance under the Bermuda Economic Substance Act 2018.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt status and cross-border organisational mismatch create perception of tax evasion or lack of substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a professional tax and substance opinion showing that the Bermuda Exempted Company is not tax resident in the UK, Gibraltar, or Bermuda if properly managed and controlled; furnish board meeting minutes, decision-making records, personnel contracts, a Gibraltar corporate-service-provider agreement, real-time platform revenue dashboards from Apple/Google, and management accounts demonstrating commercial purpose. The file must reconcile why revenue is collected through Gibraltar and demonstrate a genuine nexus to global MMORPG publishing operations rather than misuse of a zero-tax territory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital in-app payment business is categorised as online gaming or high-risk e-gaming by the bank's AML underwriting engine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a sector-specific compliance binder: final payment flows from Apple App Store and Google Play to the corporate bank account, executed merchant-of-record agreements, in-app virtual-item terms and refund policy, consumer-protection procedures, transaction-monitoring logs, SOC 2 Type II and PCI DSS Level 1 attestations, and an independent legal opinion characterising the software publishing activity under ISIC 5820 as non-gambling entertainment so that the account is not treated as a licensed remote-gambling operator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound cross-border capital injection is viewed as high-risk source-of-wealth or potential structuring path.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a board resolution authorising the capital injection, an executed equity subscription or shareholder loan agreement with pricing and repayment terms, the parent treasury's bank statements evidencing the exact source account for the preceding 12 months, an independent source-of-wealth statement signed by the ultimate beneficial owner, and a group transfer-pricing note demonstrating that the inflow is an intra-group equity contribution rather than an unexplained third-party liability. Include the intended SWIFT narrative and prior bank references so the receiving bank can match the inward MT103 to a pre-discussed reference code.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound liquidity into the Gibraltar treasury must be transmitted from the parent company's regulated bank account to the pre-boarded capital escrow account held in the name of the Bermuda Exempted Company. Use SWIFT MT103 for client credit or MT202 COV for interbank cover; include a structured purpose narrative such as 'INTRAGROUP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - EQUITY/LOAN - GB__GI__BM_EXEMPTED_CO__ISIC_5820_02_HARDCORE_MMORPG_GLOBAL' to enable automatic reconciliation. The routing reference must include the unique capital-injection number, the issuing bank's SWIFT BIC, the source jurisdiction, and the final beneficiary legal name. The remitting bank should issue an authenticated SWIFT MT199 pre-advice to the receiving treasury contact before the first transfer. Prior to the first inbound flow, the Gibraltar bank must receive an executed capital resolution and source-of-wealth confirmation; the bank will hold the remittance in the escrow sub-account and, on evidence of commercial need, release funds to the operational concentration account. Inbound flows must not be split below reporting thresholds, must never be commingled with third-party or user funds, and must be recorded against the entity's capital ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade disbursements, including developer settlements, licensing fees, cloud infrastructure payments, Apple/Google revenue-share payments, payment-gateway costs, and merchant-of-record payouts, must clear over bank-grade rails. For GBP disbursements use Faster Payments or CHAPS through the Gibraltar bank's UK correspondent; for EUR use SEPA Credit Transfer with TARGET2 settlement; for USD use the bank's US correspondent via Fedwire or CHIPS. Material disbursements must be sent by SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary legal name, address, account/IBAN, BIC, and an invoice-mapped purpose code. Recurring beneficiaries must be pre-registered in the payable master. Commercial Letters of Credit are reserved for physical hardware procurement and, where required, a standby LC to secure an Apple/Google merchant-credit facility; LCs are not used for recurring digital royalties. The treasury must apply a four-eye approval rule, match each outbound payment to a VAT/commercial invoice, retain SWIFT confirmations, and sweep residual balances to the interest-bearing GBP/EUR/USD concentration account daily.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in GIP/GBP/EUR/USD up to the 12-month forecasted operating cash-flow budget, executed under an umbrella ISDA with a GFSC-licensed bank or credit institution
Covered FX swaps for fund-sweep reconciliation and intercompany convertible-loan exposure, including principal-and-interest swaps
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in emerging-market currencies encountered by global MMORPG users, where the local currency is not freely deliverable to a Gibraltar account, with USD settlement
European-style options, both calls and puts, in GBP/USD and EUR/USD to hedge platform-payout volatility and cap adverse budget deviation
Cross-currency swaps for longer-term intercompany financing with a UK or Gibraltar group treasury counterparty, subject to board approval and IFRS valuation
USD floating-to-fixed swaps only where the underlying cash-flow stream is generated from actual dollar-denominated app-store net revenue and where no speculative trade is undertaken

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the end of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of BMD 1,000; administrative strike-off if outstanding after 6 months of the due date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of BMD 5,000 per non-compliance; potential strike-off for persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Economic Substance Authority / Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the end of the accounting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial penalty of BMD 10,000 and BMD 200 per day of continuing default; possible strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return (Overseas or Non-Resident Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the annual return date (anniversary of incorporation or previous annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of GBP 100; automatic warning notice after 90 days; strike-off if not resolved within 9 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 42 days after the annual return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to GBP 500 per day; disqualification of directors for serious or repeated contraventions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the accounting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of up to GBP 500,000 and imprisonment of officers for deliberate non-compliance; additional GBP 500 per day during default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, due with the Gibraltar Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may lead to deemed resident status, imposition of 10% corporate tax, and late payment interest.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: In Bermuda, no statutory audit is required for a private exempted company unless it is a 'permit company', a public company, or exceeds the medium-sized company thresholds. Under Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, an audit becomes compulsory if the company is 'large' (turnover > GBP 10.2M, balance sheet total > GBP 5.1M, or average employees > 50). A global MMORPG publisher with material in-app purchase revenue may exceed these thresholds and accordingly trigger a mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Gibraltar accounts must be prepared under IFRS as adopted by the EU or UK GAAP (FRS 101/102). Bermuda statutory accounting records may be prepared under IFRS or US GAAP; no public filing of financial statements is required for a private exempted company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For each shareholding transfer, the Register of Members must be updated and proper instrument duly executed; Gibraltar requires the filing of an annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Statement with any changes in PSC/UBO details. Bermuda requires the filing of a Beneficial Ownership Change Notice within 30 days of any shareholding transfer that alters the ultimate beneficial ownership.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 – 25,000 (mandatory audit triggered by large-company thresholds; waived if qualifying as micro/small in both jurisdictions)
